Saying: God won't give you more than you can handle
WhatItMeans: People take it as a promise that God caps every hardship at what they can bear, so no suffering will ever be more than they can cope with.
WhatTheBibleSays: The verse behind it, 1 Corinthians 10:13, is about temptation, not suffering: God "will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able" and makes a way of escape. About suffering Paul says the opposite: he and his companions were "pressed out of measure, above strength" (2 Corinthians 1:8), and it happened so they would trust God rather than themselves (2 Corinthians 1:9). I hold that the saying, meant as comfort, can wound: when life is genuinely more than someone can handle, it tells them God broke a promise He never made, instead of pointing them to the God who carries what we cannot.
Origin: A modern folk paraphrase that stretches 1 Corinthians 10:13, swapping "temptation" for suffering in general. No single author or date is known for the wording.
